changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: For engineering-led buyers, pitch to the engineering leader and make a hands-on build an explicit step: 'Build a working flow in our sandbox this week.' Frame the payoff as giving the team its time back, in the buyer's words, for example 'Payments shouldn't be a team' and 'We want to stop babysitting this.'
changes.why: The deal stopped being a bake-off when a customer engineer built a working sitter payment flow in our sandbox, the VP of Engineering owned the decision, and the buyer's pain was two engineers tied up on upkeep, not anything our developer line says.

changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: Stop leading with the acceptance-rate slide for low-ticket marketplace buyers. Use that slot for the sandbox invitation and the seller onboarding and local payout story.
changes.why: The acceptance-rate slide was delivered in full and met silence, and the buyer dismissed it outright: 'our average booking is 38 dollars, I'm not losing sleep over auth rates.'

changes.current_line: Onboard, verify and pay out to sellers worldwide, in their local currency.
changes.change: For marketplace buyers, use the buyer's own word for seller payments instead of 'payouts' (Fetchwell said 'sitter pay'), and lead with getting sellers paid locally as they launch new countries. Prepare a one-line answer for finance on whether and how seller payout timing changes, and confirm it with product before making any timing promise.
changes.why: M11's onboarding and local-currency story drew interest, but the customer never says 'payouts', and the CFO's only question was 'does this change when sitters get paid?', which nothing in our pitch answered.

changes.change: Add a 'what do we lose' proof point for buyers switching providers: a clear statement on keeping PayPal and Venmo and migrating saved cards, plus a named reference at comparable size. Get a definitive Venmo position from product or solutions engineering first, because we did not have one.
changes.why: Mid-evaluation the buyer's questions turned to 'Do we lose PayPal, do we lose Venmo, what happens to the saved cards', the rep had no Venmo answer, and the requested reference of 'who's done this at our size without losing cards?' was never delivered.
